newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rise on hopes strike set to end.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rise on hopes strike set to end.

text.p: French shares rose on Thursday as investors were heartened by the dollar's gains and gambled on a rapid end to an 11-day truck drivers' strike.
Brokers said the market was also boosted by a squeeze on short positions and hopes of a drop in the franc after a string of comments by French officials on the mark-franc exchange rate.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 19.95 points or 0.9 percent at 2,290.72 at midday, while the CAC-40 futures contract was 16.5 points higher at 2,290.50. Volume was 2.3 billion francs.

Shares in insurer AGF and steelmaker Usinor rose amid speculation they were the candidates to take the place of UAP in the CAC-40 index. UAP is set to be removed from the index as a result of its planned merger with insurer Axa.
Cie Generale des Eaux rose 0.63 percent after chairman Jean-Marie Messier told the Financial Times the group expects 1997 profits of at least four billion francs.
Luxury goods group LVMH rose 1.3 percent after the company confirmed it had struck an agreement to buy around 55 percent of Chateau d'Yquem, one of France's most prestigious vineyards.
LVMH did not disclose the price, but an industry expert estimated the pricetag for 100 percent of the vineyard at one billion francs.
